harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate so the application keeps writing to the same file handle after rotation). Verified with a forced rotation that the inode is preserved and appends work post-rotation. Completed mandatory single-node restart evidence: captured healthy baseline, rebooted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified logrotate config, log data, rotated archive, and crond all recovered intact.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no long-running app process holds it open (static log written by a one-shot inventory job)
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily rotation, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Forced rotation with logrotate -vf and confirmed same inode retained, .gz archive created, and post-rotation append succeeded
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, log state, config, crond status)
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed
Verified post-restart recovery: logrotate config intact, app.log and app.log.1.gz intact, crond active, logrotate -d still validates cleanly

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations, app continues writing after rotation (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: logrotate.d/inventory created with daily/rotate 7/compress/copytruncate; debug and forced-rotation runs show correct behavior, same inode after rotation, and successful append to app.log post-rotation
Captured boot_id 6aa805ba..., log contents, directory listing, and logrotate config prior to reboot
systemctl reboot scheduled and acknowledged; subsequent poll still showed old boot_id then a connection timeout confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed to 1f931121-be0b-47fb-a0af-165e4a3da362, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of log rotation config and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory, app.log, app.log.1.gz, and crond service all verified intact and functional; logrotate -d dry run still validates the config
